subject: Nimble on a SLURM managed cluster: how to optimize use?

messages.author: 4a248770402c04bc
messages.subject: Nimble on a SLURM managed cluster: how to optimize use?
parts:
I'm working on moving my Nimble modeling from my laptop to the SLURM managed cluster at our university and I'm trying to wrap my head around how I should do things differently. How much resources should I request in terms of nodes, cpus, tasks, and memory? Are there ways I should be trying to parallelize things that aren't as obvious as separate jobs? Can Nimble take advantage of GPUs? I wish I had more specific questions about all this, but at this point I don't yet know enough to know what to ask!

Any advice, guidance, or references to such would be appreciated.

Cheers,
Gregory

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Nimble on a SLURM managed cluster: how to optimize use?
parts:
hi Gregory,

The main thing is that if you want to parallelize across MCMC chains or some other algorithm applied to a given model, you need to create separate copies of the model (via nimbleModel()), compiled model, and uncompiled and compiled algorithm (e.g., the MCMC). I.e., do not do "model2 <- model1", as nimble models and algorithms are copied by reference, so model2 would just point to the same model values as model1. (We're working on enhancements that will allow for easier parallelization, but for now, that's how things are.)

As far as nodes/cpus/tasks, I would just think of each MCMC chain as a separate SLURM task. As far as memory, it's really a matter of how much a given model+algorithm needs.

And, no we don't provide support for GPUs.

-chris
